findings.body:
bump() takes `let mut v = self.value.lock().unwrap()` at line 13 and keeps that guard alive until the function returns, since MutexGuard has a Drop impl and is not released early. At line 15 it calls self.get(), which at line 9 calls `self.value.lock()` on the same non-reentrant std::sync::Mutex. The thread tries to lock a mutex it already holds, so it blocks forever (or panics, depending on the platform). This happens on every bump() call.

Trigger: Any call to Counter::bump().

Impact: Every call to bump() hangs the calling thread permanently (or panics on platforms that detect re-entry). Any caller of bump() is affected, and the thread that holds the lock cannot recover.
findings.suggestion: Drop the guard before calling get(), or return the value from the guard directly: `let mut v = self.value.lock().unwrap(); *v += 1; *v`.
findings.title: bump() self-deadlocks by calling get() while holding the mutex guard

risk_level.reason: bump() still holds the mutex guard `v` while calling self.get(), which likely locks the same non-reentrant Mutex again and would deadlock.
